newsitem.title: USA: Boeing extends rebound after earnings battering.
newsitem.headline: Boeing extends rebound after earnings battering.

text.p: Shares of Boeing Co continued to firm Wednesday after being clobbered Monday, following the company's disappointing first quarter earnings and a warning that its shift to newer aircraft models would likely pressure near-term profit margins.

Boeing lost 6-3/4 to close at 95-1/4 on Monday but has risen since then as investors looked at the company's long-term prospects, analysts said. Boeing was up 2-3/4 to 98-7/8 in midday trading Wednesday.
"There are some challenging issues in 1997, but it all comes together in 1998," said Byron Callan, an aerospace analyst with Merrill Lynch.

Callan was surprised by the extent of the market's negative reaction to Boeing's weaker-than-expected first quarter results. Boeing posted operating earnings of $0.87 a share, compared with a consensus analysts estimate of $1.00 a share, according to First Call.
Callan said Boeing's higher research and development costs were more disappointing than the actual first quarter results.

"I was more disappointed by the reason for the shortfall. R&D should be more predictable than that. There could be a deeper story going on there. There could be some other costs that were attributed to the R&D," Callan said.
Adding to Boeing's woes on Monday, media reports suggested that Boeing competitors Lockheed Martin Corp and Airbus Industrie may merge. Lockheed later denied the report.
Wolfgang Demisch, an aerospace analyst with BT Securities Corp, said the market's "sharp reaction to the first quarter represents a buying opportunity of some value."
On Wednesday, Demisch upgraded Boeing to a strong buy from a buy.
Shares of Boeing started to rebound Tuesday as it said it will build a $9 billion network of communications satellites as part of partnership with Teledesic Inc.
Teledesic is a communications firm mostly-owned by Microsoft Corp Chairman Bill Gates and Craig McCaw, who built the world's largest cellular telephone company.
Boeing will invest up to $100 million in Teledesic, giving it a 10 percent stake in the privately-held company.
This move will launch Boeing's "relatively unknown satellite business into the major league," Lehman Brothers analyst Joseph Campbell said in a research report.
The Teledesic project also marks another major move by new Boeing chief executive Phil Condit to broaden the company's business base, Campbell said.

The satellite venture only adds to other positives surrounding Boeing, such as the planned acquisition of McDonnell Douglas Corp and the recent acquisition of a Rockwell International Corp unit, analysts said.

"There is no reason to ask, ever again, what Boeing's peak earnings are going to be. Phil Condit...is going to make Boeing into the next GE (General Electric Co ) and its earnings are likely to rise indefinitely," Campbell said.
Other analysts were pleased by Boeing's reiterated forecast for 340 jet aircraft deliveries this year, which is up more than 50 percent from 218 in 1996.
